tool.name: hicPrepareQCreport
tool.description: summarizes the QC of several hicBuildMatrix runs

tool.help:
QC report of several Hi-C libraries ===================================
**hicPrepareQCreport** (also installed as **hicQC**) reads the QC log files that **hicBuildMatrix**, **hicBuildMatrixMicroC** or **hicQuickQC** write for each library and summarizes them in one HTML report with tables and plots. This allows the quality of several libraries to be compared side by side.
_________________
Usage -----
Add one *QC log file* per library: the raw QC output of **hicBuildMatrix** (QC.log). Each library gets a *Label* in the tables and plots; without a label the dataset name is used. All logs must contain the same QC lines, so logs of **hicBuildMatrix** and of **hicBuildMatrixMicroC** cannot be combined in one report.
The report shows, per library, the number of sequenced reads, the fraction of mappable, unique and high quality pairs, the pairs discarded for being dangling ends, self ligations, same fragment, self circles or duplicates, the fraction of inter-chromosomal, short range (< 20 kb) and long range contacts, and the read pair orientations. An explanation of each measure is given in the help of **hicBuildMatrix**.
**PASS/WARN/FAIL report (HiCExplorer 4)**
With *Create a PASS/WARN/FAIL report* an additional self-contained HTML report is written that judges five metrics per library: valid pairs, inter-chromosomal contacts, duplicated pairs, dangling ends and self-ligated pairs. A value on the accepted side of its cutoff, or exactly on it, is PASS; a value past the cutoff by at most 20 % of the cutoff is WARN; a value further past it is FAIL. The 20 % margin is fixed. The default cutoffs for valid pairs (25 % of sequenced reads) and inter-chromosomal contacts (10 % of valid pairs) follow the HiCExplorer usage guidance ("usually 25%-40% of the reads are valid"; "good Hi-C libraries have lower than 10% inter chromosomal contacts"). The cutoffs for duplicated pairs, dangling ends and self-ligation have no published HiCExplorer standard and are conservative starting points. The report needs no JavaScript: its charts are drawn as plain HTML tables and its navigation uses anchor links, so it is displayed completely under Galaxy's default HTML sanitization, without the administrator having to allowlist this tool. An optional inline script only adds a theme toggle, collapsible sections and sortable tables, and is removed by the sanitizer.
_________________
Output ------
- The QC report (HTML) with the plots. - The QC table with all measures per library, and four tables with the values of the plots: unmappable and non-unique pairs, discarded pairs, contact distances and read orientation. - Optionally, the PASS/WARN/FAIL report (HiCExplorer 4).
_________________
For more information about HiCExplorer please consider our documentation on readthedocs.io_.
.. _readthedocs.io: http://hicexplorer.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html
